title: Which carbon accounting tasks can you hand to AI without failing an audit?
summary: Which carbon accounting tasks AI can take over, which need a person, and what evidence an assurance provider will ask for at each step.
body_markdown:
You can hand AI any carbon accounting task whose output can be checked against a written rule: reading utility bills, mapping files to templates, matching activities to emission factors and flagging anomalies. Keep people on anything that needs judgement about the business, such as boundaries, methods, material estimates and sign-off.


> **Key takeaways**
> • If a wrong answer would break a rule you can write down, AI can do the task. If the right answer depends on how your business works, a person decides.
> • An assurance provider will ask whether each figure traces to a source, who reviewed it and what has changed since.


IBM's Institute for Business Value found that companies spend 43% more on sustainability reporting than on sustainability innovation ([Beyond checking the box , 2024](https://www.ibm.com/thought-leadership/institute-business-value/en-us/report/sustainability-business-value) ). We build AI for carbon and climate management, and the first question teams ask us is whether their auditor will accept the result. The answer depends on three problems that eat much of that budget.


## Where does carbon accounting time actually go?


**Utility bills arrive as PDFs that don't match your reporting period.** A bill runs 14 March to 12 April, shows an estimated read and lists two meters. Splitting the kWh across the days in the reporting period is rule-based work that AI does well. The provider will check whether estimated reads were later replaced with actuals.


**Scope 3 forces a trade-off between spend-based and supplier-specific data.** Spend-based estimates multiply what you paid by an industry-average factor, so a price rise shows up as an emissions rise. Supplier figures are closer to reality, yet each supplier draws its boundary differently. AI can match spend lines to factors and chase suppliers, but choosing the method for your largest categories is a call you will have to defend.


**Assurance is becoming mandatory, and it starts limited.** Australia's assurance standard requires limited assurance on Scope 1 and 2 emissions in year one and reasonable assurance on all climate disclosures by year four ([Grant Thornton, ASSA 5010](https://www.grantthornton.com.au/insights/blogs/final-phasing-for-mandatory-sustainability-assurance-released/) ). The IAASB's global standard, ISSA 5000, applies to periods beginning on or after 15 December 2026. Limited assurance leans on inquiry, so expect questions about your process before any testing.


## What should AI do, and what evidence will an auditor want?


When we design AI for these steps, we follow one rule: nothing is saved until the data owner confirms it, and anything the AI can't place goes to a person.


Task Rule or judgement? Evidence the auditor will ask for


Extract and map data from bills and supplier files Rule. AI does it, a person reads the rows that fail Original document linked to every figure


Match activities to emission factors Rule for most lines. Judgement for material categories Factor, source, version and the reason for any override


Set boundaries, methods and estimates Judgement Written methodology, approved by a named person


Lock the period and sign off Judgement Who locked it, when, and every change made afterwards


## Where do AI-assisted inventories fail assurance?


The failure we see most often is a human decision nobody recorded. A 40% rise in electricity at one site gets flagged, someone confirms it is a new production line, and the explanation stays in an email. The figure was right and still became a finding.


The second is an unexplained factor change. If a category moves from a spend-based factor to a supplier figure, "the tool chose it" will not satisfy the provider. Record the reason when the change is made.


## How should a VP of Sustainability prepare?


We ask customers to put three questions to any figure or statement in their disclosure. Where did it come from? Who checked it? What has changed since the first version? If your process answers all three without anyone searching an inbox, AI can take on more. If not, fix the record-keeping first, because AI produces numbers faster than teams can document them.


## FAQ


**Will auditors accept emissions data processed by AI?** Assurance providers test evidence and controls, whoever produced the figure. AI-processed data holds up when each figure traces to its source and every review and change is logged.
